text: So if there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort from love, any fellowship in the Spirit, any affection and mercy,
then make my joy complete: be of one mind, having the same love, united in spirit, intent on one purpose.
Do nothing out of selfish ambition or empty conceit, but in humility consider one another better than yourselves.
Let none of you look only to your own interests, but each of you also to the interests of others.
Have this mind among yourselves, which was also in Christ Jesus,

versions.text: Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus,
versions.explanation: The Greek relative clause has no verb, and both readings are possible: "which is yours in Christ Jesus" (relational) or "which was also in Christ Jesus" (exemplary). Since verses 6-8 present Christ's self-humbling as the pattern to imitate, the exemplary reading fits the flow of the passage better; if the current wording is kept, a footnote noting the alternative would help the reader.

text: who, existing in the form of God, did not count equality with God something to be grasped,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men. And being found in appearance as a man,

versions.text: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in human likeness. And being found in appearance as a man,
versions.explanation: γενόμενος means "becoming/being made," not specifically "born" (Paul uses γεννάω elsewhere for birth). "Made in the likeness of men" keeps the parallel with "taking the form of a servant" and avoids importing a nativity nuance not in the Greek.

text: he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.
Therefore God has highly exalted him and given him the name that is above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
Therefore, my beloved, as you have always obeyed—not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence—work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
for it is God who works in you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
so that you may be blameless and innocent, children of God without fault in the midst of a crooked and twisted generation, among whom you shine like lights in the world,
holding fast the word of life. Then I can boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
But even if I am poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice, and I rejoice with all of you.
In the same way you also should rejoice, and rejoice with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged by news of you.
I have no one else like him, who will genuinely care about your welfare.
For they all seek their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know his proven worth: like a son with his father, he has served with me in the gospel.
So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me,
and I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon as well.
Still, I thought it necessary to send you Epaphroditus—my brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger and minister to my need—
since he has been longing for all of you and was distressed because you heard that he was ill.
Indeed he was ill, close to death. But God had mercy on him, and not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
So I am all the more eager to send him, that you may rejoice at seeing him again and my own sorrow may be eased.
Welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
because he came near to death for the work of Christ, risking his life to make up for the help you could not give me.
